learningGoals.title: Turn `promotionGtidExecuted` and `divergentGtid` into a defensible lost-transaction count
Write an incident record that separates what was measured from what was assumed
Rehydrate the failover record from its two durable copies the way the operator does

config.title: The post-failover audit report
config.description: Build `braudit`: a tool that turns a captured MysqlFailoverGroup status into an incident record — when the promotion happened, from which site to which, the promotion GTID, each site's divergent set, and a verdict of RPO 0, N transactions lost, or UNMEASURED. Every number is computed from the GTID sets, so the figure you put in the ticket is one you measured.
config.instructions:
## How this works

`playground` failed over. `pdx` took writes about twelve seconds after you held `iad` down, and the
incident review wants a number. `braudit` turns one captured status into an incident record: when the
promotion happened, which site it moved to, the promotion GTID, the divergent set held by every other
site, and a verdict — `RPO 0`, `N transactions lost`, or `UNMEASURED`.

Capture the artefact from your own playground:

```bash
kubectl -n bloodraven-playground get mysqlfailovergroup playground -o json > playground-after-failover.json
python3 braudit.py playground-after-failover.json
```

No cluster to hand? `tests/fixtures/playground-recovery-blocked.json` is that capture, taken after the
promotion this unit drove, with `iad` back and blocked on four divergent transactions.

The arithmetic is the operator's own. There is no divergence exactly when the new primary's GTID set
contains the old primary's; what it does not contain is the difference, `GTID_SUBTRACT(old, new)`, and
the cardinality of that difference is your lost-transaction count. You compute it here, from the sets,
for every site that is not the active one — including the reader, which is where a site that came up
writable for a few seconds before the sidecar fenced it will show up.

## Your tasks

**TODO A — `parse_gtid_set(text)`.** Return `{uuid: [(start, end), ...]}`. Accept several UUIDs
separated by commas, several intervals for one UUID separated by colons (`uuid:1-19:25-30`), a
single-transaction interval written bare (`uuid:7`), and newlines anywhere, because a captured set is
folded across lines. Empty string gives `{}`. Anything else raises `ValueError` — including a MySQL 9.x
tagged set such as `uuid:Domain_1:1-3`, because a tag is part of the UUID's identity and quietly
dropping it would understate the count.

**TODO B — `transaction_count(gtid_set)`.** The number of transactions in a parsed set. An interval
`(20, 23)` is four transactions, not one and not three.

**TODO C — `gtid_subtract(minuend, subtrahend)`.** `GTID_SUBTRACT`: the transactions in the first set
that are not in the second. Subtracting from the middle of an interval splits it —
`{u: [(1, 32)]}` minus `{u: [(1, 19), (25, 30)]}` is `{u: [(20, 24), (31, 32)]}`, which is seven
transactions. A replica's `gtid_executed` really does look like that mid-catch-up with a parallel
applier, so this is not a contrived case.

**TODO D — `select_failover_record(obj, now)`.** The operator writes the failover record twice, to the
status subresource and to the `bloodraven.shipstream.io/last-failover` /
`bloodraven.shipstream.io/last-failover-target` annotation pair, because the two paths fail
independently. Rehydrate it the way the operator does after a restart: discard a copy stamped more
than five minutes ahead of `now`, discard a copy whose target is not a site in `spec.sites`, take the
later of what survives, and give a tie to status — equal instants describe the same promotion. Return
`{"at": datetime|None, "target": str, "source": "status"|"annotations"|"none"}`.

**TODO E — `audit(obj, now)`.** Build the record. Apply the verdict rules in this order and stop at the
first that matches:

1. The active site is missing from `status.sites`, or its `gtidExecuted` is empty → `UNMEASURED`.
2. `status.promotionGtidExecuted` is empty → `UNMEASURED`. The failover step that records it is
   non-fatal, so a promotion can complete without it, and a capture without it cannot be audited.
3. The active site's `gtidExecuted` does not contain `promotionGtidExecuted` → `UNMEASURED`. The site
   writing now is not the site this record describes.
4. Any non-active site has an empty `gtidExecuted` → `UNMEASURED`. An unknown site is not a zero.
5. Total is 0 → `RPO 0`.
6. Otherwise → `N transactions lost`.

## What the scaffolding is for

Argument parsing, capture loading, `parse_time`/`fmt_time`, `render_gtid_set`, `render` and the exit
plumbing are wired. So is `gtid_contains`, written as `not gtid_subtract(subset, superset)` — it is
there to show that containment is subtraction asked the other way round, which is why TODO C buys you
both halves of the operator's test.

## Expected output

```text
$ python3 braudit.py tests/fixtures/playground-recovery-blocked.json --now 2026-04-30T21:00:00Z
group: bloodraven-playground/playground
failoverAt: 2026-04-30T20:55:52Z
recordSource: status
from: iad
to: pdx
promotionGtidExecuted: a2cc879c-5f9d-11f1-9fae-8e47bc2a4544:1-19,a3c3f9e8-5f9d-11f1-bf37-568bfb8d0365:1-7
site: iad divergent=a2cc879c-5f9d-11f1-9fae-8e47bc2a4544:20-23 lost=4
site: reader divergent=- lost=0
lost: 4
verdict: 4 transactions lost
$ echo $?
1
```

Exit `0` for `RPO 0`, `1` when transactions were lost, `2` for `UNMEASURED`.

## Rules

- **Count from the sets, never from the count.** `status.sites[].divergentTransactionCount` and
  `status.sites[].divergentGtid` are the operator's own answer, published only once it has fenced the
  returning site and run the comparison. Half the captures you will audit were taken before that
  existed. Read neither as an input; if you print them at all, print them as a cross-check.
- Verdict strings are exact: `RPO 0 — no transaction was lost`, `4 transactions lost`
  (`1 transaction lost` in the singular), `UNMEASURED — <reason>`.
- `promotionGtidExecuted` in the report is the captured set rendered through `render_gtid_set`, so the
  folded newline disappears.
- `from` is the non-active site holding the most divergent transactions, or `-` when nothing diverged.
  Nothing in the status records which site was demoted; divergence is the only evidence you have.
- Standard library only. No cluster access at grading time.
- Audit before you reclone. A capture taken after the reclone shows no divergence, because the
  divergent transactions are gone — that is what a reclone is.

starterCells.content:
### The record `audit()` returns

| key | value |
| --- | --- |
| `group` | `<namespace>/<name>` from `metadata` |
| `failoverAt` | the winning record's instant, `fmt_time`d, or `-` |
| `recordSource` | `status`, `annotations`, or `none` |
| `from` | the non-active site with the most divergent transactions, else `-` |
| `to` | the winning record's target, else `-` |
| `promotionGtidExecuted` | `status.promotionGtidExecuted` through `render_gtid_set`, else `-` |
| `sites` | one `{"name", "divergent", "lost"}` per non-active site, in status order |
| `lost` | the measured total, or `None` when `UNMEASURED` |
| `verdict` | one of the three exact strings |
| `exitCode` | `0` RPO 0, `1` lost, `2` unmeasured |

`render()` already turns this into the report. It is the dict the tests read.

### The two facts this whole tool rests on

**Step 6 of the failover sequence** runs `SELECT @@global.gtid_executed` on the candidate before it
accepts a single write, and records the answer in `status.promotionGtidExecuted`. That step is
**non-fatal**: if the read errors, the operator logs a warning and promotes anyway. A promotion with no
promotion GTID is a legal outcome, and an audit that invents a number for it is worse than one that
refuses.

**The divergence comparison** is `newPrimaryGtid.Contains(oldPrimaryGtid)`, and when it fails,
`oldGtid.Subtract(newGtid)` with a transaction count taken from the difference. The operator runs it
against a GTID re-read taken *after* a defensive fence, so the set cannot grow underneath the
comparison. You are running the same subtraction against a capture, which is why a capture is a
snapshot and not a stopwatch: audit the one you took, and say which one you took.

steps.title: Get a capture worth auditing
steps.description: Drive the emergency failover on `playground` again if the playground is up, then save `kubectl -n bloodraven-playground get mysqlfailovergroup playground -o json`. If you have no cluster, use `tests/fixtures/playground-recovery-blocked.json`, which is the same capture after the promotion this unit drove. Run `python3 braudit.py <capture>` before you change anything: the starter reports `RPO 0` against a capture that plainly shows four divergent transactions.
steps.completionCriteria: A capture file exists whose `.status.lastFailoverTarget` and `.status.promotionGtidExecuted` are both non-empty, and `python3 braudit.py <capture>` prints a line beginning `group: ` and exits without a traceback.

steps.title: Parse a GTID set and count it (TODO A, TODO B)
steps.description: Implement `parse_gtid_set` and `transaction_count`. Handle several UUIDs, several intervals per UUID, a bare single-transaction interval, and the newlines a captured set is folded across. Refuse a tagged set rather than mis-counting it.
steps.completionCriteria: `python3 -c "import braudit as b; print(b.transaction_count(b.parse_gtid_set('u:1-5:9-11,v:7')))"` prints `9`, and `python3 -c "import braudit as b; b.parse_gtid_set('u:Domain_1:1-3')"` exits non-zero with a `ValueError`.

steps.title: Implement GTID_SUBTRACT (TODO C)
steps.description: Return the transactions of the first set that are not in the second, splitting an interval when the subtrahend sits inside it. This one function gives you both halves of the operator's test: the difference, and — through the wired `gtid_contains` — containment.

steps.title: Rehydrate the failover record (TODO D)
steps.description: Read both durable copies, apply the five-minute future-clock guard and the `spec.sites` membership check, take the later survivor, and give a tie to status. The starter ships the naive status-only read; `playground-annotation-newer.json` is the capture where that read names the wrong site and the wrong minute.

steps.title: Assemble the record and the verdict (TODO E)
steps.description: Compute each non-active site's divergent set against the active site's `gtidExecuted`, count it, and apply the six verdict rules in order. Three outcomes, three exit codes: measured loss, measured zero, and unmeasurable.
steps.completionCriteria: `python3 braudit.py tests/fixtures/playground-recovery-blocked.json --now 2026-04-30T21:00:00Z` prints `verdict: 4 transactions lost` and exits 1; the same command on `playground-clean-rejoin.json --now 2026-05-02T05:25:00Z` prints `verdict: RPO 0 — no transaction was lost` and exits 0; on `playground-no-promotion-gtid.json --now 2026-05-02T05:20:00Z` it prints a line starting `verdict: UNMEASURED — ` and exits 2.

steps.title: Name the field you did not read
steps.description: Run the tool against `tests/fixtures/playground-early-capture.json`. It reports eight lost transactions, and that capture carries no `divergentTransactionCount` on any site — the old primary is still unreachable, so the operator has not run its comparison yet. A tool that had read the field would have reported RPO 0 and closed the incident. Record that in the source: add a comment at the top of `braudit.py` naming the field you did not read and the capture that shows why.
steps.completionCriteria: `braudit.py` contains a comment line mentioning `divergentTransactionCount`, and `python3 braudit.py tests/fixtures/playground-early-capture.json --now 2026-05-02T05:18:00Z` prints `lost: 8`.

rubric.criterion: The count is measured from the GTID sets
rubric.description: Every reported count comes from `transaction_count(gtid_subtract(...))` over sets parsed out of the capture. `status.sites[].divergentTransactionCount` and `status.sites[].divergentGtid` are never read as inputs (printing them as a labelled cross-check is fine). Subtraction handles multi-interval sets and interval splitting; a set that cannot be parsed raises rather than counting wrong. Full marks require the early-capture fixture — no operator-computed divergence anywhere in it — to report 8.

rubric.criterion: The failover record is rehydrated as the operator rehydrates it
rubric.description: Both durable copies are read; a copy more than five minutes ahead of `now` is discarded; a copy whose target is not in `spec.sites` is discarded; the later survivor wins; a tie goes to status. `recordSource` names which copy was used, so a reader can tell a status read from an annotation read. A submission that reads only status caps at half these marks even if it is otherwise correct.

rubric.criterion: Three verdicts, applied in order, with matching exit codes
rubric.description: `RPO 0`, `N transactions lost` and `UNMEASURED` are distinct outcomes with exit codes 0, 1 and 2. All four unmeasurable conditions are implemented and are checked in the stated order: no active-site `gtidExecuted`, no `promotionGtidExecuted`, an active site that does not contain the promotion GTID, and any non-active site with no `gtidExecuted`. `UNMEASURED` carries a reason naming the field or site that was missing. No submission that prints a number for an unmeasurable capture can score above half here.

rubric.criterion: Craft: legible under incident conditions, loud on bad input
rubric.description: The report reads top to bottom as an incident record and needs no explanation at 3am: one fact per line, per-site lines showing the actual divergent set beside its count. Functions are small and single-purpose, with the parsing, the arithmetic, the record selection and the verdict separable. Malformed input produces an exception or an `UNMEASURED` verdict naming the problem — never a silent zero, never a traceback with no message. Comments explain the non-obvious rules (the tie, the skew guard, the field not read), not the syntax.

testCases.name: canonical_audit_of_playground
testCases.code:
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "tests")
from harness import audit, run_cli, line, braudit, fixture
fails = []
def check(cond, msg):
    if not cond:
        fails.append(msg)

PROMO = ("a2cc879c-5f9d-11f1-9fae-8e47bc2a4544:1-19,"
         "a3c3f9e8-5f9d-11f1-bf37-568bfb8d0365:1-7")

r = audit("playground-recovery-blocked.json", "2026-04-30T21:00:00Z")
check(r["lost"] == 4, "lost=%r want 4" % (r["lost"],))
check(r["verdict"] == "4 transactions lost", "verdict=%r" % (r["verdict"],))
check(r["exitCode"] == 1, "exitCode=%r want 1" % (r["exitCode"],))
check(r["failoverAt"] == "2026-04-30T20:55:52Z", "failoverAt=%r" % (r["failoverAt"],))
check(r["recordSource"] == "status", "recordSource=%r want status" % (r["recordSource"],))
check(r["from"] == "iad", "from=%r want iad" % (r["from"],))
check(r["to"] == "pdx", "to=%r want pdx" % (r["to"],))
check(r["promotionGtidExecuted"] == PROMO,
      "promotionGtidExecuted=%r (fold the captured newline away)" % (r["promotionGtidExecuted"],))

sites = dict((s["name"], s) for s in r["sites"])
check(set(sites) == set(["iad", "reader"]),
      "sites=%r want one entry per non-active site" % (sorted(sites),))
check(sites.get("iad", {}).get("divergent") == "a2cc879c-5f9d-11f1-9fae-8e47bc2a4544:20-23",
      "iad divergent=%r" % (sites.get("iad", {}).get("divergent"),))
check(sites.get("iad", {}).get("lost") == 4, "iad lost=%r want 4" % (sites.get("iad", {}).get("lost"),))
check(sites.get("reader", {}).get("lost") == 0, "reader lost=%r want 0" % (sites.get("reader", {}).get("lost"),))
check(sites.get("reader", {}).get("divergent") == "-", "reader divergent=%r want -" % (sites.get("reader", {}).get("divergent"),))

c = audit("playground-clean-rejoin.json", "2026-05-02T05:25:00Z")
check(c["lost"] == 0, "clean rejoin lost=%r want 0" % (c["lost"],))
check(c["verdict"] == "RPO 0 \u2014 no transaction was lost", "clean verdict=%r" % (c["verdict"],))
check(c["exitCode"] == 0, "clean exitCode=%r want 0" % (c["exitCode"],))
check(c["from"] == "-", "clean from=%r want -" % (c["from"],))

code, out = run_cli("playground-recovery-blocked.json", "2026-04-30T21:00:00Z")
check(code == 1, "CLI exit=%r want 1 when transactions were lost" % (code,))
check(line(out, "verdict") == "4 transactions lost", "CLI verdict line=%r" % (line(out, "verdict"),))
check(line(out, "lost") == "4", "CLI lost line=%r" % (line(out, "lost"),))
code, out = run_cli("playground-clean-rejoin.json", "2026-05-02T05:25:00Z")
check(code == 0, "CLI exit=%r want 0 for RPO 0" % (code,))

print("PASS" if not fails else "FAIL: " + " | ".join(fails))
testCases.description: Correctness on the canonical capture: the post-failover `playground` status with `iad` blocked on four divergent transactions. Checks the full record — group, failover instant and source, from/to, the normalised promotion GTID, the per-site divergent sets and counts, the total, the verdict string and the exit code — and checks the clean-rejoin capture reports RPO 0 with exit 0.

testCases.name: gtid_arithmetic_and_unmeasurable_captures
testCases.code:
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "tests")
from harness import audit, run_cli, line, braudit, fixture
fails = []
def check(cond, msg):
    if not cond:
        fails.append(msg)

b = braudit()
for name in ("parse_gtid_set", "transaction_count", "gtid_subtract", "select_failover_record", "audit"):
    check(callable(getattr(b, name, None)), "missing required function %s()" % name)

g = b.parse_gtid_set("u:1-5")
check(isinstance(g, dict) and list(g) == ["u"], "parse_gtid_set('u:1-5') keys=%r" % (list(g),))
check([tuple(iv) for iv in g.get("u", [])] == [(1, 5)],
      "parse_gtid_set('u:1-5')['u']=%r want [(1, 5)]" % (g.get("u"),))

check(b.transaction_count(b.parse_gtid_set("u:1-5:9-11,v:7")) == 9, "multi-interval + bare seqno count")
check(b.transaction_count(b.parse_gtid_set("u:1-19,\nv:1-7")) == 26, "folded newline count")
check(b.transaction_count(b.parse_gtid_set("")) == 0, "empty set counts 0")
check(b.transaction_count(b.parse_gtid_set("u:42")) == 1, "single-transaction interval counts 1")

sub = b.gtid_subtract(b.parse_gtid_set("u:1-32"), b.parse_gtid_set("u:1-19:25-30"))
check(b.render_gtid_set(sub) == "u:20-24:31-32", "split subtraction rendered %r" % (b.render_gtid_set(sub),))
check(b.transaction_count(sub) == 7, "split subtraction count=%r want 7" % (b.transaction_count(sub),))
check(b.render_gtid_set(b.gtid_subtract(b.parse_gtid_set("u:1-9"), b.parse_gtid_set("u:1-9,v:1-3"))) == "-",
      "subtracting a superset must leave nothing")
check(b.render_gtid_set(b.gtid_subtract(b.parse_gtid_set("u:1-3"), b.parse_gtid_set("v:1-3"))) == "u:1-3",
      "a different UUID subtracts nothing")

try:
    b.parse_gtid_set("a2cc879c-5f9d-11f1-9fae-8e47bc2a4544:Domain_1:1-3")
    fails.append("a tagged GTID set must raise ValueError, not be silently mis-counted")
except ValueError:
    pass
except Exception as exc:
    fails.append("tagged set raised %s, want ValueError" % type(exc).__name__)

u = audit("playground-no-promotion-gtid.json", "2026-05-02T05:20:00Z")
check(u["verdict"].startswith("UNMEASURED"), "missing promotion GTID verdict=%r" % (u["verdict"],))
check(u["lost"] is None, "missing promotion GTID lost=%r want None" % (u["lost"],))
check(u["exitCode"] == 2, "missing promotion GTID exitCode=%r want 2" % (u["exitCode"],))
code, out = run_cli("playground-no-promotion-gtid.json", "2026-05-02T05:20:00Z")
check(code == 2, "CLI exit=%r want 2 when unmeasurable" % (code,))
check(line(out, "lost") == "-", "CLI lost line=%r want - when unmeasurable" % (line(out, "lost"),))

def drop_iad_gtid(obj):
    for s in obj["status"]["sites"]:
        if s["name"] == "iad":
            s["gtidExecuted"] = ""
m = audit("playground-recovery-blocked.json", "2026-04-30T21:00:00Z", drop_iad_gtid)
check(m["verdict"].startswith("UNMEASURED"),
      "a site with no gtidExecuted cannot be measured, verdict=%r" % (m["verdict"],))
check(m["exitCode"] == 2, "unmeasurable site exitCode=%r want 2" % (m["exitCode"],))

def promo_beyond_active(obj):
    obj["status"]["promotionGtidExecuted"] = "a2cc879c-5f9d-11f1-9fae-8e47bc2a4544:1-99"
w = audit("playground-recovery-blocked.json", "2026-04-30T21:00:00Z", promo_beyond_active)
check(w["verdict"].startswith("UNMEASURED"),
      "active site not containing the promotion GTID must be UNMEASURED, got %r" % (w["verdict"],))

print("PASS" if not fails else "FAIL: " + " | ".join(fails))
testCases.description: Generality on awkward input, plus the structural check that the four required functions exist by name and are independently callable with the documented shapes. Multi-interval sets, bare single-transaction intervals, folded newlines, disjoint UUIDs, a tagged set that must raise `ValueError`, and the three unmeasurable captures: no `promotionGtidExecuted`, a site with no `gtidExecuted`, and an active site that does not contain the promotion GTID.

testCases.name: catches_trusting_the_operators_divergence_fields
testCases.code:
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "tests")
from harness import audit, run_cli, line, braudit, fixture
fails = []
def check(cond, msg):
    if not cond:
        fails.append(msg)

cap = fixture("playground-early-capture.json")
for s in cap["status"]["sites"]:
    check("divergentTransactionCount" not in s and "divergentGtid" not in s,
          "fixture sanity: the early capture must carry no operator-computed divergence")

r = audit("playground-early-capture.json", "2026-05-02T05:18:00Z")
check(r["lost"] == 8, "lost=%r want 8 (7 on iad, 1 on reader)" % (r["lost"],))
check(r["verdict"] == "8 transactions lost", "verdict=%r" % (r["verdict"],))
check(r["exitCode"] == 1, "exitCode=%r want 1" % (r["exitCode"],))
check(r["from"] == "iad", "from=%r want iad" % (r["from"],))

sites = dict((s["name"], s) for s in r["sites"])
check(sites.get("iad", {}).get("divergent") == "a2cc879c-5f9d-11f1-9fae-8e47bc2a4544:20-24:31-32",
      "iad divergent=%r want the two-interval difference" % (sites.get("iad", {}).get("divergent"),))
check(sites.get("iad", {}).get("lost") == 7, "iad lost=%r want 7" % (sites.get("iad", {}).get("lost"),))
check(sites.get("reader", {}).get("divergent") == "b7f01a44-5f9d-11f1-8c21-0242ac110004:1",
      "reader divergent=%r want the one transaction it took while briefly writable"
      % (sites.get("reader", {}).get("divergent"),))
check(sites.get("reader", {}).get("lost") == 1, "reader lost=%r want 1" % (sites.get("reader", {}).get("lost"),))

def lying_count(obj):
    for s in obj["status"]["sites"]:
        if s["name"] == "iad":
            s["divergentTransactionCount"] = 99
            s["divergentGtid"] = "a2cc879c-5f9d-11f1-9fae-8e47bc2a4544:20-118"
l = audit("playground-recovery-blocked.json", "2026-04-30T21:00:00Z", lying_count)
check(l["lost"] == 4, "with a stale divergentTransactionCount=99 the audit must still measure 4, got %r"
      % (l["lost"],))

code, out = run_cli("playground-early-capture.json", "2026-05-02T05:18:00Z")
check(code == 1, "CLI exit=%r want 1" % (code,))
check(line(out, "lost") == "8", "CLI lost line=%r want 8" % (line(out, "lost"),))

print("PASS" if not fails else "FAIL: " + " | ".join(fails))
testCases.description: Catches a shortcut: reading `status.sites[].divergentTransactionCount` or `divergentGtid` instead of subtracting the GTID sets. The early capture was taken while the old primary was still unreachable, so the operator has published neither field — a shortcut reports RPO 0 for a capture holding eight lost transactions, seven on `iad` across a split interval and one on the reader from the seconds it came up writable. A second case plants a stale `divergentTransactionCount` of 99 beside sets that say 4.

testCases.name: catches_status_only_failover_record
testCases.code:
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "tests")
from harness import audit, run_cli, line, braudit, fixture
fails = []
def check(cond, msg):
    if not cond:
        fails.append(msg)

r = audit("playground-annotation-newer.json", "2026-05-02T05:40:00Z")
check(r["failoverAt"] == "2026-05-02T05:34:11Z",
      "failoverAt=%r want the newer annotation stamp" % (r["failoverAt"],))
check(r["to"] == "iad", "to=%r want iad" % (r["to"],))
check(r["recordSource"] == "annotations", "recordSource=%r want annotations" % (r["recordSource"],))
check(r["from"] == "pdx", "from=%r want pdx" % (r["from"],))
check(r["lost"] == 3, "lost=%r want 3" % (r["lost"],))
check(r["exitCode"] == 1, "exitCode=%r want 1" % (r["exitCode"],))

def skewed(obj):
    obj["metadata"]["annotations"]["bloodraven.shipstream.io/last-failover"] = "2026-05-02T05:50:00Z"
s = audit("playground-annotation-newer.json", "2026-05-02T05:40:00Z", skewed)
check(s["failoverAt"] == "2026-05-02T05:17:03Z",
      "an annotation stamped more than 5 minutes ahead of now must be discarded, got %r" % (s["failoverAt"],))
check(s["to"] == "pdx" and s["recordSource"] == "status",
      "after discarding the skewed annotation the status copy wins, got to=%r source=%r"
      % (s["to"], s["recordSource"]))

def unknown_target(obj):
    obj["metadata"]["annotations"]["bloodraven.shipstream.io/last-failover-target"] = "sfo"
t = audit("playground-annotation-newer.json", "2026-05-02T05:40:00Z", unknown_target)
check(t["to"] == "pdx" and t["recordSource"] == "status",
      "a target absent from spec.sites invalidates that copy, got to=%r source=%r" % (t["to"], t["recordSource"]))

def no_annotations(obj):
    obj["metadata"]["annotations"] = {}
n = audit("playground-annotation-newer.json", "2026-05-02T05:40:00Z", no_annotations)
check(n["recordSource"] == "status" and n["to"] == "pdx",
      "with no annotations the status copy is the record, got source=%r to=%r" % (n["recordSource"], n["to"]))

def tie(obj):
    obj["metadata"]["annotations"]["bloodraven.shipstream.io/last-failover"] = obj["status"]["lastFailover"]
q = audit("playground-annotation-newer.json", "2026-05-02T05:40:00Z", tie)
check(q["recordSource"] == "status", "equal timestamps describe one promotion: ties go to status, got %r"
      % (q["recordSource"],))

print("PASS" if not fails else "FAIL: " + " | ".join(fails))
testCases.description: Catches a shortcut: reading `status.lastFailover`/`lastFailoverTarget` alone, which is what the starter ships. In this capture the status write was the one that failed, so the annotation pair is newer and the status copy names the previous promotion — a status-only tool reports the wrong site and a seventeen-minute-old instant. Also checks the guards that make the other direction safe: a skewed future annotation and a target absent from `spec.sites` are discarded, and an exact tie goes to status.
